weaknesses.title: Weight-11 result is logically inconsistent with the reported failed PSLQ run, and the headline overclaims
weaknesses.detail: The title and abstract promise results 'up to weight 11', but the weight-11 claim covers only a 6-function sub-basis chosen by 'human-guided exploration'. That sub-basis is a subset of the full 12-element basis, so the relation found on it (largest coefficient 38016) is also a relation on the full basis. A PSLQ run on the full basis at up to 64 digits that 'found no relation' therefore contradicts the existence of the sub-basis relation. This points to a flawed search setup, or to a spurious sub-basis relation. The explanation 'precision too low relative to coefficient height' is not credible: the known relation has height of about 4e4 and was found at 32 digits. The statement that the full-basis dimension is 'undecided' also ignores the trivial lower bound of at least 1. Because the sub-basis was selected by hand, the dimension-1 claim there says nothing about the true weight-11 relation space. The weight-6 case also failed, so the 'weights 3, 5, 7, 9, 11' framing amounts to odd weights only, with the largest case incomplete.
weaknesses.suggestion: Rewrite the title and abstract to state only what was shown: a relation exists at weight 11, so the full-basis dimension is at least 1. Drop or correct the precision explanation. Then rerun the full-basis PSLQ with enough digits (or a lattice-reduction / exact linear-algebra method). Explain why the full-basis search missed a relation that lies inside its span. Explain how the sub-basis was chosen.

weaknesses.title: Evidence is purely numerical, the exact check is weak, and the completeness criterion is shaky
weaknesses.detail: Every relation rests on 4 verifier points at 32 digits. The only exact check is the vanishing of the leading Laurent coefficient y^w. That check cannot test the ζ(w) coefficient or the subleading terms, and the full Laurent polynomial is known in closed form. The 'dimension exactly one' claims rest on singular-value gaps. The smallest retained singular values shrink with weight (0.73, 0.037, 1.3e-4, 8.6e-7, 4.4e-6) and approach the 1e-8 cutoff, which is arbitrary. The weight-6 case already failed (smallest large singular value 2.44e-8, no singular value below 1e-24), which shows the criterion is fragile. The matrix sizes (6x3, 7x4, 9x6, 12x9, 9x6) do not match '4 verifier points' or the stated seeds, and the paper never explains how rows are generated. The dimension claims also depend on a basis that excludes products of Eisenstein series such as E2E5 and E3E4. Known weight-7 and weight-9 identities involve these products, so 'full dihedral basis' is misleading. The verifier and generator belong to the same automated pipeline, so independence is limited.
weaknesses.suggestion: Check the entire Laurent polynomial exactly. Use many more points, including points with larger τ2. Justify the singular-value cutoffs with a documented error model and report how the rows are built. Redefine 'full basis' honestly as the basis of C, E and ζ only. Where possible, upgrade key relations to proofs via the known sieve or iterated-Eisenstein-integral algorithms.

weaknesses.title: Paper is not self-contained: definitions, normalisations and evaluation method are missing
weaknesses.detail: The Model section never actually defines C(a,b,c) or E(w). The lattice-sum formula is garbled ('with weight factor ... with weight w=a+b+c' with nothing between), and the normalisation of E(w) and the ζ(w) coefficients (π factors) are not stated. The coefficients 960, 2160, 8640 and so on are meaningless without them. The numerical method for evaluating the two-loop lattice sums to 32 digits, which is the heart of the 'trusted base', is not described. The finite-difference Laplacian check is not credible as stated. Fourth-order differences with h=1e-6 at 32 digits have round-off of about eps/h^2 ≈ 1e-20, yet residuals of 1e-25 are reported. The text also contains a garbled sentence ('For the identity of, the terms lie in...').
weaknesses.suggestion: State the explicit definitions of C(a,b,c), E(w) and the Laplacian normalisation. Describe the evaluation algorithm and its working precision (internal precision must exceed 32 digits for the residuals to be meaningful). Give an error analysis for the Laplacian. Repair the garbled sentences.

weaknesses.title: Contribution is thin: most results are known, new ones have unresolved novelty, and results are duplicated
weaknesses.detail: The relations at weights 3, 5 and 7 and all Laplace equations are textbook results (Green–Russo–Vanhove, D'Hoker–Green–Vanhove, D'Hoker–Green, D'Hoker–Kaidi, Basu). Yet the weight-3 and weight-5 novelty is labelled 'inconclusive' because search engines disagreed, which is not a scholarly argument. The weight-9 relation, the only possibly new content besides weight 11, is acknowledged as 'may be implied' by Gerken–Kleinschmidt–Schlotterer and Gerken's basis-decomposition package. The paper never uses these methods to settle the question, although they are directly applicable. The 'not found in 85 abstracts' novelty argument for weight 11 is weak. Results are also padded. Observation 5 repeats Observation 4, Observation 11 repeats Observation 3, Examples 12 and 13 repeat Observations 1 and 2, and Observation 10 follows trivially from Observations 9 and 2 (L C(2,2,1) = 8E(5) together with 30C(2,2,1) = 12E(5) + ζ(5)). This inflates the count of '24 verified statements'. Observations 3 and 11 cite different sources for the same identity.
weaknesses.suggestion: Cite the known results and present the weights 3, 5, 7 cases and the Laplace equations as validation of the method. Compare the weight-9 and weight-11 relations explicitly with the output of Gerken's package or the GKS generating series, to decide novelty. Merge the duplicate observations and drop Observation 10 as a corollary. Report the numbers of independent claims accurately.

weaknesses.title: Holomorphic section is disconnected from the main topic and contains imprecise or doubtful statements
weaknesses.detail: Propositions 14–17 (Jacobi identity, E8/D16 lattices, Δ and j, eta-quotient spans) are classical and have no logical link to the modular-graph-function question. Proposition 17 is a table of dimensions of eta-quotient spans that overlaps with known work (Rouse–Webb on spaces spanned by eta quotients). The 'targeted search of 33 abstracts' does not establish novelty. The word 'exhaustive' is unjustified, since eta quotients form an infinite family and the search bound on the exponents is not stated. Prop. 14(ii) treats θ^2 as weight 1 on Γ0(4) with trivial character, but θ^2 has the nontrivial character χ_{-4}. The lattice should be the glued D16^+, not D16, to give a modular theta series, and Prop. 15 lists duplicated and redundant identities (θE8 = E4 appears twice). The Jacobi identity is credited to an unrelated 2026 paper instead of Jacobi's classical result. The remark that 'Sturm bound 1 is exceeded' by q^0..q^11 is far from sharp and adds nothing. The appendix counts of counter-checks (2 passed, 27 'did not pass', 1 not executable) are confusing, and the provenance table uses German labels and mismatched numbering.
weaknesses.suggestion: Move the holomorphic section to an appendix as validation of the Sturm-bound machinery, or cut it. Fix the character and the D16^+ terminology and remove the duplicated identities. State the exponent search bounds for Proposition 17 and compare with Rouse–Webb. Cite the classical sources. Clarify the counter-check statistics and tidy the provenance table.
